analysis.title: FX and Rates Sentiment Survey: Rates vs risk switcheroo
key_insights: BofA argues respondents worry about consensus longs in risk but should worry about consensus longs in rates. Almost 40% of respondents name long rates as their highest-conviction view, and global duration positioning is close to an all-time high.

63% of respondents think 'long risk' is the most consensus view into 2027. BofA says investors may underestimate how crowded long duration hedges have become and points to last week's price action as evidence of crowded rate longs.

Duration extensions are visible in USD, EUR (core Europe) and GBP. US duration positioning is modestly overweight and at its most bullish level this year, and the gap versus core Europe has narrowed toward neutral.

Peripheral Europe duration positioning recovered but remains bearish. Most respondents expect the 10y OAT-Bund spread to peak at 175-200bp with risks skewed to the upside, which BofA says could leave France vulnerable in 2027, especially if spreads tighten into year-end on a successful budget adoption.

After the sharp October correction, EM positioning has started to recover in both FX and rates. Rates exposure jumped even as sentiment continued to deteriorate, and cash positions in EM portfolios keep rising.

Investors moved from neutral to moderately overweight EM local-currency debt versus EM external debt in November. Positioning in EM hard-currency debt is now neutral, and investors shifted from underweight to overweight in EM external debt versus other HY debt.

USD sentiment and positioning turned bearish again after last month's recovery. On a longer time frame USD bearishness stands out, while GBP bullishness and EUR bearishness stand out versus last year.

The Bull-Bear index shows EUR FX positioning turned neutral, GBP positioning recovered to neutral for the first time since October 2025, and JPY longs were somewhat reduced even as JPY sentiment hit new YTD highs.
Three-quarters of respondents see AI market pricing as at least modestly above what future earnings justify, with half seeing it as well above. Views on AI's 2027 growth impact skew bearish.

42% expect an AI sentiment wobble to come with a weaker USD. Strong US data is the most likely driver of USD strength (54%), while softer US data (42%) and a faltering AI rally (25%) are the leading drivers of USD weakness.

Improved growth remains the main driver of global long-end rate moves since end-June, though fiscal concerns and hyperscaler supply have gained traction. In the long end, steepeners are now favoured over flatteners in both EUR and US rates.
Most respondents expect at most verbal ECB intervention if long-end EGB yields rise again. Most expect the OAT-Bund spread peak in 1Q 2027.
Most respondents still see a BoJ terminal rate of 2.25% or higher as needed to stabilise the JPY. About a quarter see the BoJ as behind the curve, but JPY views skew modestly bullish.

A plurality sees oil at $125-150/bbl for more than three months as enough to trigger a sharp consumer slowdown. Average cash levels in portfolios are at 3% and risk appetite is stable at normal levels.

tension_points.bull_case: Respondents see long risk as the most consensus view (63%) and the most crowded trade, while long rates are their highest-conviction trade (almost 40%). Duration extensions in USD, EUR and GBP back the long-rates view.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA argues long rates are the real consensus position, with global duration near an all-time high and last week's price action showing crowded rate longs.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Recent US data have likely challenged the long-rates conviction. BofA states no specific level.

tension_points.bull_case: Spreads could tighten into year-end on a successful budget adoption.
tension_points.bear_case: Most respondents expect a peak at 175-200bp with upside-skewed risks, and BofA says France could be vulnerable in 2027 despite periphery duration extensions.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Successful budget adoption with spreads tightening into year-end.

theme_stances.key_argument: Investors may underestimate how consensus their own concern about risk exposures is, and so how crowded long duration hedges have become.
theme_stances.evidence: worry about consensus longs in rates

theme_stances.key_argument: Periphery duration extensions conflict with upside-skewed spread expectations, leaving France vulnerable in 2027.
